method: each day solved independently by NSGA-II (no learning across days); decision vector x in {0,1,2}^(24h x 10 houses) -> share fraction [0%, 50%, 100%]
objectives: F1 = mean comfort (max), F2 = std of comfort (min)
caveat: on sunny days (wf=1.0, ~85%) comfort objectives saturate (comfort=1.0, std=0.0 for every action vector) -> NSGA-II has no selective pressure and argmax(F1-F2) returns an arbitrary but reproducible policy; on cloudy days (wf=0.5) NSGA-II genuinely optimizes. See weather_split_metrics.csv.
env: identical to main OCEAN-MARL runs (demand profiles, ring topology, battery start 50%, weather generator)
